originalTitle: Bill Miller's investing strategy: How the legendary fund manager outperformed the market for 15 straight years
simplifiedContent: Bill Miller, a well-known investor, was able to do better than the overall stock market for 15 years in a row. He achieved this by using a strategy that involves buying stocks at a low price and waiting for a long time for them to increase in value. Miller looks for stocks that are undervalued, meaning they are priced lower than they should be, and waits for the market to correct itself. This approach, which combines patience and careful stock selection, allowed Miller to outperform the market. By following this strategy, Miller was able to make smart investment decisions and achieve long-term success.

originalTitle: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank posts Rs 34 crore Q1 loss; asset quality stress persists
simplifiedContent: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank recently reported a loss of Rs 34 crore for the quarter ending June, which is the fifth time in a row they've lost money. This loss happened because the bank has many loans that aren't being paid back, which is known as "asset quality stress". Even though the bank's loss is smaller than before, it's still a problem that many of its loans aren't being repaid, with 6.1% of its total loans being trouble loans. This is important because it affects the bank's overall performance and ability to make money. The bank's continued losses and high number of bad loans are concerns for its financial health.

originalTitle: Muthoot Finance reports 25% rise in Q1 profit, announces leadership transition
simplifiedContent: Muthoot Finance, a company that lends money to people using their gold as security, made a profit of Rs 2,550 crore in the first quarter of the year. This is 25% more than what they made during the same time last year. The increase in profit is mainly due to the growth in their gold loan business. The company also announced that Alexander George Muthoot will become the new managing director starting October 1, pending approval from the company's shareholders. This news is important because it shows how well the company is doing and who will be leading it in the future.

originalTitle: Week Ahead: Wall Street eyes US jobs data, SpaceX debut earnings and Disney results
simplifiedContent: This week, investors are waiting to see how many new jobs were created in the US in July. This information is important because it will help them understand what might happen to interest rates in the coming months. Interest rates affect how much it costs to borrow money, which can impact the stock market. Investors will be watching this closely to make informed decisions about their investments. The jobs report is considered one of the most important economic releases of the week, and it will be closely watched by those on Wall Street.

originalTitle: Sebi order against Zee likely to delay planned  ₹3,143-crore fundraise
simplifiedContent: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has made a decision that will affect Zee. Sebi has stopped Zee from buying or selling stocks and securities for a certain amount of time. This decision is likely to delay Zee's plans to raise ₹3,143 crore, which is a large amount of money. This matters because Zee was counting on raising this money, and now they may have to wait. The delay may impact Zee's plans and activities, at least for now.

originalTitle: Yen Traders Brace for More Intervention With US at Japan’s Side
simplifiedContent: Some important people who trade money, called currency traders, are waiting to see what happens next with the Japanese yen. Last week, Japan and the US worked together to help the yen, and it made the yen's value go back up quickly. These traders think that Japan and the US might work together again to help the yen, and they're getting ready for this to happen when markets open in Asia on Monday. This matters because it could affect the value of the yen and how it trades with other countries' money. It's a big deal for people who invest in or trade with the yen, so they're paying close attention to what happens next.
